parameters.name: Pressure waveform
parameters.explanation: The pressure trace displays airway pressure over time. Assess the measured pressures, including plateau pressure when appropriately obtained, and PEEP including intrinsic PEEP; interpret changes alongside patient effort and mechanics.

parameters.name: Flow waveform
parameters.explanation: The flow trace shows the direction and speed of gas movement during breathing. Failure of expiratory flow to reach baseline before the next inspiration may suggest incomplete exhalation; review with the respiratory team rather than diagnosing from a single trace.

parameters.name: Volume
parameters.explanation: Tidal volume is the volume associated with a breath. Compare set and measured exhaled values and document tidal volume relative to predicted body weight; leaks and pressure limits may affect delivery.

parameters.name: Respiratory rate
parameters.explanation: Breath frequency observed during ventilation. Compare the displayed total rate with the prescribed mandatory rate where applicable and the patient's respiratory effort; the relationship varies with mode and triggering.

safety_concepts.text: Go to the patient immediately when an alarm occurs. If ventilation is inadequate, summon emergency help and support effective ventilation according to the unit emergency protocol in parallel; do not delay rescue while identifying the alarm cause.
Do not change alarm limits or modes unless authorised by order, protocol and training; extreme limits make alarms useless.

monitoring_concepts.text: Record set and delivered values, airway pressures, SpO2, end-tidal CO2 and waveforms at the policy frequency, and trends.

Assess plateau pressure, measured tidal volume relative to predicted body weight, PEEP and auto-PEEP as appropriate with the respiratory team; this is monitoring guidance, not a universal prescription.

escalation_concepts.text: Call for help early for rising pressures, falling volumes, desaturation or distress.
